title: Psalms Chapter 75 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 75 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 75 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 75.

questions.question: To whom is thanks given in Psalms 75:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:1 states, 'Unto thee, O God, do we give thanks.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 75:2, what will happen when the congregation is received?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:2 says, 'When I shall receive the congregation I will judge uprightly.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist say he bears up in Psalms 75:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:3 states, 'I bear up the pillars of it.' referring to the earth.

questions.question: Who is warned in Psalms 75:4 not to deal foolishly?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:4 says, 'I said unto the fools, Deal not foolishly.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 75:4, what are the wicked instructed not to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:4 states, 'and to the wicked, Lift not up the horn.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 75:1 declares that God's name is far away from His wondrous works.
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:1 says, 'for that thy name is near thy wondrous works declare.' so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 75:2, judgment will be carried out unfairly.
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:2 states, 'I will judge uprightly,' meaning judgment will be fair.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 75:3 mentions that all the inhabitants of the earth are dissolved.
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:3 says, 'The earth and all the inhabitants thereof are dissolved.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 75:5 commands to lift up your horn on high.
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:5 says, 'Lift not up your horn on high,' so the statement is false.

questions.question: In Psalms 75, which command comes first?
options: Lift not up your horn on high
questions.explanation: The first instruction in Psalms 75 is to give thanks to God (verse 1) before the other commands appear.

questions.question: What does the psalmist say about the earth in Psalms 75:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:3 says, 'I bear up the pillars of it,' referring to the earth being supported.

questions.question: According to Psalms 75:4, who is told not to lift up the horn?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:4 instructs 'to the wicked, Lift not up the horn.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 75:6, from where does promotion NOT come?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:6 states, 'promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south.'

questions.question: Who is described as the judge in Psalms 75:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:7 says, 'But God is the judge.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 75:8, what is in the hand of the LORD?
options: A cup full of red wine
questions.correctAnswer: A cup full of red wine
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:8 states, 'For in the hand of the LORD there is a cup, and the wine is red; it is full of mixture.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 75 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 75 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 75:5, what attitude should believers avoid displaying?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:5 instructs believers to 'Lift not up your horn on high: speak not with a stiff neck,' meaning they should avoid prideful and stubborn attitudes.

questions.question: Where does Psalms 75:6 say promotion does NOT come from?
options: From the east, west, or south
questions.correctAnswer: From the east, west, or south
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:6 clearly states, 'For promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south,' emphasizing that human sources do not grant promotion.

questions.question: Who is identified as the judge who puts down one and sets up another in Psalms 75?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:7 states, 'But God is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another,' showing God's sovereign authority over promotion and judgment.

questions.question: What metaphor does Psalms 75:8 use to describe God's judgment?
options: A cup full of red wine
questions.correctAnswer: A cup full of red wine
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:8 describes God's judgment as 'a cup, and the wine is red; it is full of mixture,' symbolizing the severity and completeness of His judgment.

questions.question: What does Psalms 75:5 teach about humility in relation to pride?
options: Humility means speaking with a stiff neck
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:5 warns against lifting up one's horn and speaking with a stiff neck, which are symbols of pride, encouraging humility instead.

questions.question: How does Psalms 75:7-8 teach about God's control over human affairs?
options: God is uninvolved in human promotion
God is the judge who controls who is exalted or brought down
Promotion comes from the strongest nations
questions.correctAnswer: God is the judge who controls who is exalted or brought down
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 emphasize that God alone judges, setting up some and putting down others, symbolized by the cup of wine poured from His hand.

questions.question: What is the consequence described in Psalms 75:8 for the wicked of the earth?
options: They will drink the dregs of God's cup
questions.correctAnswer: They will drink the dregs of God's cup
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:8 explains that the wicked will wring out and drink the dregs of the cup in God's hand, symbolizing judgment and suffering.

questions.question: How does Psalms 75:6-7 teach believers to trust in God's sovereignty rather than worldly powers?
options: By understanding promotion comes only from God, not east, west, or south
By seeking favor from powerful nations
questions.correctAnswer: By understanding promotion comes only from God, not east, west, or south
questions.explanation: These verses show that human directions or powers do not grant promotion; God alone judges and elevates, teaching trust in His sovereignty.

questions.question: What does Psalms 75:5-6 imply about self-exaltation and reliance on human sources for promotion?
options: Self-exaltation and reliance on human promotion are discouraged
questions.correctAnswer: Self-exaltation and reliance on human promotion are discouraged
questions.explanation: Verse 5 warns against lifting up one's horn (self-exaltation), and verse 6 denies promotion from human sources, teaching humility and reliance on God.

questions.question: If a believer follows the instruction in Psalms 75:5 to 'speak not with a stiff neck,' what does Psalms 75:8 suggest will happen to the wicked who do not?
options: They will drink the dregs of God's cup
They will be forgiven without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: They will drink the dregs of God's cup
questions.explanation: Verse 5 warns against pride, and verse 8 explains that the wicked, who presumably reject this instruction, will face judgment symbolized by drinking the dregs of God's cup.

questions.question: What biblical virtue is emphasized by the warning in Psalms 75:5 against speaking with a stiff neck?
questions.explanation: Speaking with a stiff neck symbolizes stubborn pride; thus, the verse promotes humility as a key virtue.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 75:7, who determines the rise and fall of individuals?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 states clearly that God is the judge who puts down one and sets up another, highlighting divine sovereignty over human status.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 75:6 teaches that promotion can come from the north.
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:6 lists east, west, and south as places from which promotion does not come. The north is not mentioned, so the implication is that promotion does not come from human directions, including the north.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 75:8, all the wicked of the earth will drink the dregs of God's cup.
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:8 explicitly says 'all the wicked of the earth shall wring them out, and drink them,' referring to the dregs of the cup in the hand of the LORD, symbolizing judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 75:5 encourages believers to lift up their horns on high as a sign of strength.
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:5 instructs 'Lift not up your horn on high,' warning against pride and arrogance, thus discouraging such behavior.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 75 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 75.

questions.question: According to Psalms 75:9, what will the psalmist declare and sing praises to forever?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:9 states explicitly that the psalmist will declare forever and sing praises to the God of Jacob, indicating a continual praise directed to this particular designation of God.

questions.question: What will happen to all the horns of the wicked according to Psalms 75:10?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:10 declares that all the horns of the wicked will be cut off, symbolizing the removal of their power or strength.

questions.question: What does Psalms 75:10 say about the horns of the righteous?
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 75:10, the horns of the righteous shall be exalted, indicating their elevation or strengthening in contrast to the wicked.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 75:10 by contrasting the horns of the wicked and the righteous?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:10 employs antithesis by contrasting 'cut off' for the wicked's horns with 'exalted' for the righteous, highlighting opposite fates.

questions.question: The cup mentioned in Psalms 75:8 is described as being full of what?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:8 describes the LORD's cup as 'full of mixture,' which symbolizes a complex and potent judgment poured out by God.

questions.question: In Psalms 75:8, who is said to wring out and drink the dregs of the cup?
options: All the wicked of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: All the wicked of the earth
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the wicked shall wring out and drink the dregs, symbolizing their receiving the full measure of God's judgment.

questions.question: Which cross-biblical passage echoes the theme of God as judge who puts down one and sets up another, as in Psalms 75:7?
questions.explanation: Daniel 2:21 reflects the theme of divine sovereignty over rulers similar to Psalms 75:7 where God judges and exalts according to His will.

questions.question: What directional sources does Psalms 75:6 deny as origin of promotion?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:6 explicitly states that promotion does not come from the east, west, or south, emphasizing that God alone is the source.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 75:2 emphasizes that judgment will be given uprightly when the congregation is gathered.
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:2 states 'When I shall receive the congregation I will judge uprightly,' confirming the truth of this statement.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 75:3, the earth and all inhabitants remain firm and unshaken.
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:3 indicates that 'The earth and all the inhabitants thereof are dissolved,' which contradicts the statement that they remain firm.

questions.question: The Hebrew word for 'horn' in Psalms 75 symbolizes what concept in ancient Near Eastern culture?
questions.explanation: In Hebrew, 'horn' (קֶרֶן, qeren) commonly symbolizes strength and power, reflected in Psalms 75:10 where cutting off or exalting horns represents diminishing or increasing power.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme in Psalms 75:9 of eternal praise to the God of Jacob?
questions.explanation: Revelation 5:13 reflects the theme of eternal praise to God, paralleling Psalms 75:9’s declaration of perpetual worship.

questions.question: How does the theme of divine judgment in Psalms 75:8 foreshadow the New Testament concept of God's wrath?
options: God’s cup of wrath poured out on the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: God’s cup of wrath poured out on the wicked
questions.explanation: The 'cup' imagery in Psalms 75:8 foreshadows the New Testament portrayal of God's wrath, such as in Revelation 14:10 where the cup of God's wrath is poured on the wicked.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares the theme of God as the ultimate judge who controls elevation and humiliation, similar to Psalms 75:7?
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2:7 speaks of the LORD raising up the poor and bringing down the mighty, paralleling Psalms 75:7’s theme of divine judgment and elevation.

questions.question: Which literary feature is demonstrated by the repetition of 'Unto thee do we give thanks' in Psalms 75:1?
questions.explanation: The repetition in Psalms 75:1 is an example of parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device emphasizing the act of giving thanks to God.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 75 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 75 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by the statement 'The earth and all the inhabitants thereof are dissolved: I bear up the pillars of it'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:3 shows God's power in sustaining the earth and its inhabitants, revealing His omnipotence as He upholds the pillars of creation.

questions.question: What does Psalms 75:2 teach about God's role when He 'receives the congregation'?
options: He blesses the righteous without judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:2 states that when God gathers His people, He judges them with righteousness, affirming His role as a just judge.

questions.question: According to Psalms 75:6-7, from where does promotion come, and who is the ultimate judge that sets up one and puts down another?
options: Promotion comes from the east; the king is the judge
Promotion comes from the west; the people judge
Promotion comes from God; God is the judge
Promotion comes from the south; the priests are the judges
questions.correctAnswer: Promotion comes from God; God is the judge
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 clarify that promotion does not come from any human direction but solely from God, who judges and raises or lowers individuals.

questions.question: What is symbolized by the 'cup' in the hand of the LORD in Psalms 75:8, and what does the 'dregs' represent?
options: The cup symbolizes blessing; the dregs represent the righteous
The cup symbolizes judgment; the dregs represent the wicked who must drink judgment
The cup symbolizes salvation; the dregs represent sin forgiven
The cup symbolizes wrath; the dregs represent angels
questions.correctAnswer: The cup symbolizes judgment; the dregs represent the wicked who must drink judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:8 uses the metaphor of a cup full of mixed wine to represent God's judgment, with the dregs being the portion the wicked wring out and drink, symbolizing their punishment.

questions.question: Which doctrine is chiefly illustrated by the cutting off of the horns of the wicked and the exaltation of the horns of the righteous in Psalms 75:10?
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:10 teaches the doctrine of divine justice, showing God's righteous judgment by humbling the wicked and lifting up the righteous.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God is indifferent to human pride and wickedness. What does Psalms 75:4-5 actually teach about God's stance on human arrogance?
options: God encourages pride to test the wicked
God warns fools and the wicked not to act arrogantly or lift their horns
God rewards the proud for their strength
questions.correctAnswer: God warns fools and the wicked not to act arrogantly or lift their horns
questions.explanation: Verses 4-5 explicitly show God's admonition against foolish and proud behavior, indicating His active opposition to human arrogance, contradicting the sceptic's claim.

questions.question: How does Psalms 75:1 reveal God’s nearness in relation to His wondrous works?
options: God is distant and unseen despite His works
God's name is near, and His wondrous works declare His presence
God's works are hidden and mysterious
God's nearness is unrelated to His works
questions.correctAnswer: God's name is near, and His wondrous works declare His presence
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:1 affirms God's nearness by stating His name is near and that His wondrous works declare this closeness and involvement with His creation.

questions.question: What theological truth is conveyed by the combined teaching of Psalms 75:9 and Psalms 75:10 regarding worship and justice?
options: God's justice is separate from worship
Praise to God is eternal, and justice involves the exaltation of the righteous
Justice is temporary and unrelated to worship
questions.correctAnswer: Praise to God is eternal, and justice involves the exaltation of the righteous
questions.explanation: Verse 9 expresses a commitment to eternal praise, while verse 10 connects this praise with God's just action of cutting off the wicked and exalting the righteous, showing worship and justice intertwined.

questions.question: What is the significance of God being described as the one who 'putteth down one, and setteth up another' in Psalms 75:7 in the context of divine sovereignty?
options: God's sovereignty is limited to Israel only
God arbitrarily favors some without reason
God exercises sovereign control over human affairs and authority
God allows humans to decide who is exalted
questions.correctAnswer: God exercises sovereign control over human affairs and authority
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:7 emphasizes God's sovereign power to raise or lower individuals, demonstrating His control over earthly authority and human destinies.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted by the declaration 'But I will declare for ever; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob' in Psalms 75:9?
questions.explanation: The commitment to eternal praise in Psalms 75:9 reflects God's faithfulness, as the psalmist testifies to God's enduring covenant love with Jacob and his descendants.

questions.question: What does the exhortation 'Deal not foolishly' in Psalms 75:4 teach about human responsibility before God’s judgment?
options: Humans are free to act foolishly without consequence
Humans are warned to act wisely and humbly before God’s judgment
Foolishness is a virtue in God's sight
Only the wicked must avoid foolishness
questions.correctAnswer: Humans are warned to act wisely and humbly before God’s judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:4 commands fools not to deal foolishly, indicating human responsibility to live wisely and humbly in the awareness of God's just judgment.

questions.question: How does Psalms 75:8's imagery of the 'red cup full of mixture' relate to the biblical theme of divine justice and wrath?
options: It symbolizes God's mercy and forgiveness
It represents God’s wrath mixed with justice poured upon the wicked
It depicts a celebratory feast for the righteous
It refers to a ritual cleansing
questions.correctAnswer: It represents God’s wrath mixed with justice poured upon the wicked
questions.explanation: The 'red cup' in Psalms 75:8 symbolizes the mixture of God's wrath and justice that is poured out on the wicked, consistent with the biblical theme of divine judgment.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight arises from combining Psalms 75:1's declaration of God's nearness with Psalms 75:7's assertion that God judges and exalts?
options: God is distant but indifferent to justice
God is near and exercises righteous judgment over all
God only judges the wicked secretly
questions.correctAnswer: God is near and exercises righteous judgment over all
questions.explanation: Together, these verses teach that God's nearness to His people includes His active role as righteous judge who exalts and humbles according to His justice.

questions.question: How does Psalms 75:6 challenge human ideas about the source of success and promotion?
options: Success comes from human effort in any direction
Success comes from the east, west, or south
Promotion does not come from any human direction but from God alone
questions.correctAnswer: Promotion does not come from any human direction but from God alone
questions.explanation: Psalms 75:6 denies that promotion arises from any earthly or human direction, affirming that God alone is the source of exaltation.

questions.question: What combined theological teaching about divine justice and human pride is conveyed by Psalms 75:4-5 and Psalms 75:10?
options: God ignores human pride and rewards the wicked
God opposes human pride and ultimately humbles the wicked while exalting the righteous
Pride is rewarded by God with exaltation
The righteous are cut off while the wicked are exalted
questions.correctAnswer: God opposes human pride and ultimately humbles the wicked while exalting the righteous
questions.explanation: Verses 4-5 warn against arrogance, and verse 10 confirms that God will cut off the horns of the wicked (symbols of pride and power) and exalt the righteous, demonstrating His justice against pride.
